Rashi on Pesachim 67a:10:1.english: With him - And Moses was a Levite.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:11:1.hebrew: תנאי היא - דאיכא תנא דלא מייתי ליה קרא לעשה, אלא ליתן לו מחנה שלישית:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:11:1.english: It is [a dispute between] Tannaim - For there is a Tanna who does not adduce the verse for a positive commandment, but rather to give him a third camp.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:11:2.hebrew: שלא יהו טמאין אחרים יושבין עמו - כגון זבין וטמאי מתים. למדנו לשלוחו של מצורע שהוא חמור מכולן:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:11:2.english: That other ritually impure people should not dwell with him - Such as zavin and those who are ritually impure due to [contact with] a corpse. We have [thus] learned regarding the sending out of a leper that it is more stringent than all of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:11:3.hebrew: יכול יהו זבין וטמאי מתים משתלחין למחנה אחת ת"ל ולא יטמאו את מחניהם תן מחנה לזה ומחנה לזה - מדלא כתיב "מחנה", משמע מחנה לכל אחד ואחד. והתם תרתי מחנות כתיבי: "וישלחו מן המחנה", "מחוץ למחנה תשלחום"; והאי "מחוץ למחנה" דמצורע, ליתן לו מחנה שלישית:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:11:3.english: One might [have thought] that zavin and those ritually impure from a corpse are sent to one camp; therefore the verse states: “and they shall not defile their camps” — give a camp to this one and a camp to that one - Since “camp” [in the singular] is not written, it implies a camp for each and every one. And there, two camps are written: “and let them send out of the camp” [and] “outside the camp you shall send them”; and this “outside the camp” [written] regarding a metzora is to give him a third camp.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:12:1.hebrew: אינו צריך - האי "מחוץ למחנה" ליתן לו מחנה שלישית להוציאו, דכולהו מהתם נפקי, דעל כרחך כולן חמורים זה מזה בטומאותיהן. דאי כולהו שוו לענין מחנות, לכתוב שילוח בקל, ואנא ידענא כל שכן דחמור בעי שילוח. ומדכתבינהו כולהו, ש"מ שילוחו של זה לא כשילוחו של זה:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:12:1.english: It is not necessary - [to expound] this [phrase,] "outside the camp," to assign him a third camp from which to send him out, for all of them are derived from there [Numbers 5:2], since perforce they are each more stringent than the other in their [laws of] ritual impurity. For if they were all equal with respect to the camps, let [Scripture] write sending out regarding the lenient one, and I would know all the more so that the stringent one requires sending out. And since [Scripture] wrote all of them, learn from it [that] the sending out of one is not like the sending out of another.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:12:2.hebrew: זב לא כ"ש - לקמיה פריך, מאי חומריה דזב מטמא מת:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:12:2.english: A zav — [is it] not all the more so? - Later on, [the Gemara] asks: What is the stringency of a zav over one who is impure due to a corpse?

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:15:1.hebrew: לרבות טמא שרץ - לשילוח, והוא הדין לנוגע בנבילה וכל טמאי מגע. וכיון דכתב רבוייא לטמאי מגע, לא איצטריך למיכתב זב, דחמיר מטמא שרץ, שהרי טומאה יוצאה עליו מגופו. זב אינו מטמא מחמת אונס — אם ראה מחמת מאכל ומשתה או חולי או קפיצה — כדאמר במסכת נדה בפרק בנות כותים (נדה דף לה.): "מבשרו" — ולא מחמת אונסו. ומשנינן: כי האי גוונא זב טמויי נמי מטמא, כגון טומאת טמאי שרץ, שאינו אלא טומאת ערב:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:15:1.english: To include one who is impure [from] a creeping animal - For sending out [from the camp]; and the same applies to one who touches a carcass and all those impure through contact. And since [the verse] wrote an inclusion for those impure through contact, it was not necessary to write [explicitly] a zav, who is more severe than one impure [from] a creeping animal, since impurity issues out upon him from his [own] body. A zav does not become impure due to an accident — [such as] if he had a sighting due to food and drink, or illness, or jumping — as it says in Tractate Niddah in the chapter [entitled] Benot Kutim (Niddah 35a): "from his flesh" — and not due to his accident. And we answer: In a case like this, a zav also becomes impure [from an accident], such as the impurity of those impure [from] a creeping animal, which is only an evening impurity [until nightfall].

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:1:1.hebrew: אלמא יש לך שעה שזבין ומצורעין משתלחין - מן העזרה, וטמאי מתים נכנסים לתוכה:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:1:1.english: Thus, there is a time when zavin and lepers are sent out - from the Temple Courtyard, and those impure from a corpse enter into it.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:1:2.hebrew: בטומאה - כשרוב ציבור טמאין במת, עושין פסח בטומאה, וזבין ומצורעין שבהן נדחין:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:1:2.english: In impurity - When the majority of the congregation are impure [through contact] with a corpse, they offer the Paschal lamb in [a state of] impurity, and the zavin and lepers among them are deferred.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:2:1.english: A leper is more stringent than a zav - Later, [the Gemara] explains his stringency.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:2:2.english: And what is this, etc. - [This is said] as a question.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:3:1.hebrew: לא יאכלו ממנו - דכי דייקינן "איש נדחה ואין ציבור נדחין", בטמא נפש הוא דדייקינן; גבי "איש כי יהיה טמא", לא כתיב אלא "לנפש", ובדידה דייקינן: איש — ולא ציבור. אלמא מהתם יליף, דאי מ"וישלחו" כדר"ל, זב נמי לישתרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:3:1.english: They may not eat from it - For when we infer [that] "an individual is deferred, and a community is not deferred," it is regarding one impure from a corpse that we make this inference; in the passage "If any man shall be impure" [Numbers 9:10], it is written only "by a corpse," and regarding that [verse] we infer: a man [is deferred], and not a community. Thus, [the Mishnah] derives [this rule] from there; for if [it were derived] from "and let them send out" [Numbers 5:2], as in the view of Reish Lakish, a zav should also be permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:4:1.hebrew: אלא לעולם מקרא קמא - וכדדייקינן: איש נדחה ואין ציבור נדחין. ודקשיא לך, אימא ציבור כלל לא — א"כ, דדיוקא דממעטינן ציבור מהאי דינא לחומרא ממעטינן, למאי הילכתא כתב לנפש למעוטי זבין ומצורעין? לכתוב טומאה סתם, דנשמע דבכל טומאות יחיד נדחה לשני וציבור לית להו תקנתא, דע"כ לנפש למעוטי זבין ומצורעין אתא ולאחמורי עלייהו. ואי לגבי ציבור לא מחמירו עלייהו — ולמימר דבטומאת מת הוא דאין ציבור נדחין, אלא עושין פסחיהן בטומאה, אבל בטומאת זיבה וצרעת אפילו ציבור נמי נדחין — לגבי מאן מחמיר עלייהו? וכ"ת לגבי יחיד מחמיר עלייהו, וקאמר טמא נפש הוא דאית ליה תשלומין לשני, אבל זב ומצורע אפי' נטהר בשני לית לי' תקנתא בתשלומין — והתניא: יכול לא יהו חייבין לפסח שני אלא טמא נפש כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:4:1.english: Rather, actually [it is derived] from the first verse - And as we infer: an individual is deferred [to the second Pesaḥ], whereas a community is not deferred. And as for your difficulty, "Say [that] a community [does] not [offer it] at all" — if so, that the inference by which we exclude a community from this law is an exclusion toward stringency, for what halakhic purpose did [Scripture] write "by reason of a corpse" to exclude zavin and metzora'in? Let it write impurity unspecified, so that we would learn that in all [types of] impurity an individual is deferred to the second [Pesaḥ] and a community has no remedy; for perforce "by reason of a corpse" came to exclude zavin and metzora'in and to be stringent upon them. And if regarding a community it is not stringent upon them — to say that it is only in corpse-impurity that a community is not deferred, rather they perform their Pesaḥ offerings in impurity, whereas in impurity of zivah and tzara'at even a community is also deferred — regarding whom is it stringent upon them? And if you should say [that] regarding an individual it is stringent upon them, and it says [that] it is [only] one impure by a corpse who has a make-up [offering] on the second [Pesaḥ], whereas a zav and a metzora, even if he became pure on the second [Pesaḥ], has no remedy with a make-up [offering] — was it not taught [in a baraita]: "One might think that none are obligated in the second Pesaḥ except one impure by a corpse, etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:5:1.hebrew: ת"ל איש איש - כי יהיה טמא, משמע כל טומאה, מדלא כתיב "לנפש" ברישא, א"נ "איש כי יגע במת". ש"מ למידרשי' באנפיה נפשיה הוא; "לנפש" למה לי? אלא ע"כ מיעוטא דציבור לאקולי אתא, ולמימרא דאין נדחין אלא עושין בטומאה, ומש"ה כתב "לנפש" למימר דבטומאת מת הוא דאקיל עלייהו, אבל זיבה וצרעת לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:5:1.english: Therefore, the verse states: “Any man” - [The phrase] “if he will be impure” implies any impurity, since “by reason of a corpse” is not written at the beginning, or else [it could have written] “a man who touches a corpse.” Learn from this that it is [to be] expounded on its own; [if so,] why do I [need] “by reason of a corpse”? Rather, perforce, the exclusion comes to be lenient for the community, and to say that they are not deferred, rather they offer [the Paschal lamb] in [a state of] impurity; and therefore [it wrote] “by reason of a corpse” to say that it is [specifically] regarding corpse impurity that [Scripture] was lenient with them, but [regarding] zivah and leprosy, no.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:7:1.hebrew: לפנים ממחיצתו - מחיצה שנאסר ליכנס בה, דהיינו לפני' מחומת כל ערי ישראל, כדאמר לקמן, מצורע משתלח חוץ למחנה ישראל:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:7:1.english: Within his boundary - [Meaning,] a boundary into which he is forbidden to enter, that is, within the wall of all the cities of Israel, as it says below, a leper is sent outside the Israelite camp.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:7:2.english: Exempt - From the lashes [for violating] "they shall not defile their camps."

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:8:1.hebrew: נתקו לעשה - ואע"ג דלאו בתר לאו כתיב, ע"כ לנתוקי לאוי אתא, דקי"ל לאו שניתק לעשה אין לוקין עליו. דאי לאטעוניה עשה ול"ת, הא כתב ביה עשה אחרינא: "וישלחו מן המחנה". אבל זבין וטמאי מתים לא נתקו לעשה, ואע"ג דעשה יתירי כתיבי, כל חד וחד למילתיה מדריש בספרי. ועוד, דבהאי כתיב "כל ימי אשר הנגע בו וגו'", משמע כל ימיו ב"בדד ישב" קאי — דאם עבר ונכנס, יחזור ויצא ואין בו עונש אחר, כדדרשינן "כל ימיו" דאונס את הנערה במס' מכות (דף טו.): "כל ימיו" בעמוד והחזר קאי, ומנתקינא ליה ללאוי:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:8:1.english: [The verse] transmuted it into a positive commandment - Even though it is not written after a negative commandment, perforce it comes to transmute negative commandments [into a positive commandment], as we hold that for a negative commandment that was transmuted into a positive commandment, one does not receive lashes. For if [it were only] to subject him to a positive commandment and a negative commandment, behold, another positive commandment is already written regarding it: "And they shall send out from the camp." However, zavim and those impure from a corpse were not transmuted into a positive commandment; and even though extra positive commandments are written [regarding them], each and every one is expounded for its own matter in the Sifrei. And furthermore, regarding this one [the leper] it is written, "All the days that the plague is upon him, etc.," which implies [that] all his days he remains subject to "he shall dwell in isolation" — that if he transgressed and entered, he shall return and go out, and there is no other punishment for it, just as we expound "all his days" regarding one who violates a maiden in Tractate Makkot (15a): "all his days" stands under [the rule of] "arise and take [her] back," and we [thereby] transmute the negative commandment.

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:9:1.hebrew: זב - מחיצתו הר הבית, דאסור לכנס במחנה לויה כדלקמן, שכל הטמאין אין משתלחין אלא מן העזרה לבדה, חוץ מזב ובעל קרי שמשתלחין אף מהר הבית, ומצורע משתלח אף ממחנה ישראל, דהיינו כל העיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 67a:9:1.english: A zav - His boundary is the Temple Mount, for he is forbidden to enter the Levite camp, as [will be stated] below, that all ritually impure people are sent out only from the Temple Courtyard alone, except for a zav and one who experienced a seminal emission, who are sent out even from the Temple Mount, and a leper is sent out even from the Israelite camp, which is the entire city [of Jerusalem].

Rashi on Pesachim 67a:9:2.english: Levite camp - The entire Temple Mount outside the wall of the Courtyard.

Tosafot on Pesachim 67a:14:1.hebrew: מאי חומרא דזב שכן טומאה יוצאה מגופו - ה"ה דהוה מצי למימר שכן מטמא משכב ומושב וכלי חרס בהיסט כדלקמן, אלא ניחא ליה למינקט חומרי דלא מצי למימר להו בסמוך גבי חומר בזב מבמצורע:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67a:14:1.english: "What is the stringency of a zav? That impurity issues from his body" - By the same token, [the Gemara] could have said: "Because he renders impure a couch and a seat, and an earthenware vessel by shifting [them]," as [stated] below; rather, it preferred to cite stringencies that it could not state shortly [thereafter] regarding the stringency of a zav over a metzora.

Tosafot on Pesachim 67a:8:1.hebrew: הכתוב נתקו לעשה - פי' בקו': דכתיב "כל ימי אשר הנגע בו", משמע דניתוק לאו הוא, כל ימיו "בדד ישב" — שאם עבר ונכנס יחזור ויצא, ואין בו עונש אחר, כמו "לא יוכל לשלחה כל ימיו". וקשה לר"י: דאם כן ה"ל לאיתויי רישיה דקרא בספרים. ועוד הקשה ריב"א: דלא דמי, ד"לא יוכל לשלחה כל ימיו" משמע דליכא לאו אלא כשמשלחה כל ימיו, אבל הכא לא משמע מקרא הכי. ואור"י: דהאי "נתקו לעשה" לא הוי כשאר לאו הניתק לעשה, שהעשה כתוב אחר הלאו בסמוך, משמע שלתקן הלאו בא — כמו "לא תותירו ממנו והנותר וגו'" (שמות י״ב:י׳), וכמו "לא תקח האם על הבנים" שלא תשלח (דברים כ״ב:ו׳-ז׳). אלא ה"פ "הכתוב נתקו לעשה": דכיון דכל הטמאים היו בכלל "ולא יטמאו את מחניהם", ופרט במצורע בפני עצמו עשה, אתא להוציאו מכלל האחרים לנתקו מן הלאו וליתנו בעשה; אבל היכא שאינו כתוב הלאו אלא על דבר אחד, לא מנתקינן את הלאו בעשה, אלא הוי בלאו ועשה. וקשה: דבעל קרי נמי לא לילקי אם נכנס לפנים ממחיצתו, שהכתוב נתקו לעשה, דכתיב "ויצא אל מחוץ למחנה". וי"ל: דהכא בחד קרא איכא תרי עשה — "בדד ישב", "מחוץ למחנה מושבו". והאי ניתוק עשה נראה דלא מהני אלא במחנה שלישית — דלא גרע מזב, הואיל ואיכא לאוקמי ניתוק למחנה שלישי'; ובמחנה שכינה חייב כרת, דלא גרע ממחוסר כפורים. וכן משמע בפ' כל הפסולים (זבחים דל"ב:), דקאמר: "ואי ביאה במקצת שמה ביאה, היכי מעייל ידיה לבהונות, אידי ואידי עשה שיש בו כרת הוא? א"ל: ומטונך — הואיל והותר לצרעתו, הותר לקריו". ואיכא למידחי דההיא כרבי יהודה, דלא חשיב ליה לקמן ניתוק לעשה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67a:8:1.english: The verse has transmuted it into a positive mitzva - Rashi explained [that] since it is written, "All the days wherein the plague is in him," it implies that it is a transmutation of a negative commandment — all his days "he shall dwell alone," [meaning] that if he transgressed and entered, he must turn back and leave, and there is no other punishment for it, like "he may not send her away all his days." And it is difficult for Rabbi Yitzchak: for if so, [the Gemara] should have cited the beginning of the verse in the texts. And Riva further raised a difficulty: that it is not comparable, for "he may not send her away all his days" implies that there is no negative commandment except when he sends her away all his days, whereas here it is not implied from the verse thus. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that this "transmuted it into a positive mitzva" is not like other negative commandments transmuted into a positive mitzva, where the positive commandment is written immediately after the negative commandment, [which] implies that it comes to rectify the negative commandment — like "you shall not leave any of it, and that which remains, etc." (Exodus 12:10), and like "you shall not take the mother with the young ... [rather] send [her] away" (Deuteronomy 22:6-7). Rather, this is the explanation of "the verse has transmuted it into a positive mitzva": since all impure people were included in "that they not defile their camps," and [Scripture] singled out the leper on his own with a positive commandment, it comes to remove him from the category of the others, to transmute him from the negative commandment and place him under a positive commandment; whereas where the negative commandment is written only regarding one matter, we do not transmute the negative commandment into a positive commandment, rather it is subject to both a negative and a positive commandment. And it is difficult: that one who had a seminal emission should also not receive lashes if he enters inside his boundary, for the verse has transmuted it into a positive mitzva, as it is written, "and he shall go outside the camp." And one can answer: that here, in one verse, there are two positive commandments — "he shall dwell alone," [and] "his dwelling shall be outside the camp." And this transmutation into a positive mitzva appears to be effective only in the third camp — for he is no worse than a zav, since it is possible to establish the transmutation as applying to the third camp; whereas in the Camp of the Divine Presence he is liable to karet, for he is no worse than one lacking atonement. And so it is implied in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaPesulim (Zevachim 32b), where [the Gemara] says: "And if partial entry is considered entry, how can he insert his hands for [the blood on] the thumbs, [when] both this and that are a positive commandment that carries karet? He said to him: And according to your own reasoning — since he was permitted [to enter] for his leprosy, he was permitted [to enter] for his seminal emission." And one can reject [this proof], [saying] that that [passage] follows Rabbi Yehudah, who does not consider it later on [to be] a transmutation into a positive mitzva:

Tosafot on Pesachim 67a:9:1.hebrew: זבין ובועלי נדות שנכנסו כו' - ריב"א לא גרס "ובועלי נדות" בהדי זבין, דהא אמרינן לקמן: "בועל נדה כטמא מת למחנות", ובתוספתא ליתיה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67a:9:1.english: Zavin and those who cohabit with menstruating women who entered, etc. - Riva does not have the reading "and those who cohabit with menstruating women" together with zavin, for we say later: "One who cohabits with a menstruating woman is like one who is ritually impure due to [contact with] a corpse with respect to the camps," and it is not [found] in the Tosefta.
